correctness.rationale: The global bounded cooperative dynamics and their positivity follow from explicit differential inequalities. Strict sublinearity proves the existence, uniqueness and global attraction of the positive state when the symmetric Metzler principal eigenvalue is positive; Perron-weighted comparison gives exponential extinction when negative. At the zero-eigenvalue threshold, the weighted mass derivative is nonpositive with a strictly dissipative logistic term, proving global extinction, and the stable transverse mode converges faster than center amplitude, yielding exactly tX->(a,1)/k. Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction produces the stated branch amplitude. Exact symbolic coefficients and illustrative finite trajectories were replayed from the included standalone script; experiments are not substituted for the analytical infinite-time proof.

value.rationale: In the strong-Allee source--sink regime, the isolated first patch cannot persist, so rescue by migration and its ultimate destruction by excessive dispersal is a motivated ecological question. An exact all-parameter classification identifies the nonlinear survival boundary, the previously uncovered neutral case has universal reciprocal-time decay rather than exponential decay, and an exact branch coefficient quantifies the disappearance of population at loss of rescue. The neutral asymptotics and branch slope are substantive model-specific features not mere parameter substitutions.
